adapter_evaluation.interpretation: Adding claim metadata to the prompt did not make the model reliably copy claim IDs or infer the next step and missing documents. The model should not be trusted to populate authoritative structured fields directly.
adapter_evaluation.recommended_follow_up: Prefer a hybrid architecture: derive claim ID, claim type, queue, missing-document list, next step, and mandatory human review from validated input data and deterministic rules. Restrict model use to a draft narrative summary, label it as model-generated, and require human review. Evaluate raw-model and guarded-pipeline metrics separately.

lora_qlora_training.note: Synthetic smoke fine-tuning only. Validation loss does not establish claims accuracy or suitability for real claim workflows.

implemented_capabilities: Structured output validation and mandatory human review flag
Rules baseline for routing and missing-document requests
Optional LoRA and QLoRA fine-tuning script
limitations: No real insurance/claimant data is included.
The rules baseline is deterministic and its evaluation labels are generated from the same rules.

The latest adapter achieved 100% schema validity and routing match on eight synthetic test examples, but only 50% next-step accuracy, 12.5% exact claim-ID matching, and 37.5% exact missing-document matching.
A small synthetic test set cannot support broad generalization claims.
No claim approval, denial, payout, fraud, liability, or coverage decision is made.
next_step: Implement and test deterministic guards for structured fields while preserving raw-model metrics separately. Do not use the adapter output as authoritative for real claims.
